reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through the Nov 23 close, data fresh: SPX 7,237.17, down 7.74% from its 120-day high and 4.99% below its 50-day and 1.54% below its 200-day after a +4.73% bounce day; SMH (460.18) and NVDA (165.05) both below Zone 2 despite +15.03% and +31.48% single-day gains; VIX rolled over to 26.62 from a 35.89 five-day high with HY OAS calm at 3.76 and the mechanical tally at 3 of 4 — a first bounce, not a confirmed bottom.
reaction.invalidation: The Watch stance is wrong if the standing falsifier completes — SPX weekly close above 7,300 with NVDA holding above $150 (already met at $165.05) and VIX closing below 25 (not met at 26.62) — or if HY OAS crosses 4.00, which voids the correction read the other way into a regime break.

ladder.response: Stay in Watch; no probes. The first bounce has failed — wait for the second low to form and test whether it holds.
ladder.trigger: SPX closes below Monday's 7,237, or SMH closes below 460 / NVDA below 165 — the bounce fails on the retest and the tape escalates lower

ladder.response: Treat as the trap case: do not chase. Wait for the failure-zone retest verdict — a rejection there confirms the bull trap and keeps all deployment on hold.
ladder.trigger: SPX bounces into the failure zone 7,750-7,820 or SMH into 580-600 without reclaiming Zone 2 first

ladder.response: Stand down to regime-break posture: the correction thesis is void, no tranche arms, and existing holdings are reviewed for the staged selling plan, not for adds.
ladder.trigger: HY OAS crosses 4.00, or VIX closes back above its 35.89 five-day high

ladder.response: Move to Probe on the AI stack (NVDA, AVGO, DDOG, ONTO): small, staged entries only, sized to the confirmation, not the dislocation.
ladder.trigger: SMH reclaims Zone 2 (470-505) and NVDA reclaims Zone 2 (175-185) and both hold for two closes, with VIX closing below 25

ladder.response: Move to Add: confirmed-bottom pattern complete — deploy per the ladder at Tranche A sizing into the names that reclaimed their zones.
ladder.trigger: A failed first bounce followed by a second low that holds while the 10-year falls

reaction.trapRisk: Monday's +4.73% SPX / +31.48% NVDA snap came on a single catalyst (Huang's reinstatement) with no zone reclaim, and the VIX has already re-spiked to 32.38 this morning — the classic pivot-and-fail setup. Entries do not chase the first bounce: any probe waits for a Zone 2 reclaim-and-hold or for the failed-bounce/second-low pattern, and a bounce into the failure zone (SMH 580-600, SPX 7,750-7,820) is treated as a bull trap until the retest proves otherwise.

strategyPosture: Watch. Monday's bounce is a first bounce, not a confirmed bottom: 3 of 4 mechanical signals are in, but SMH and NVDA sit below Zone 2, SPX is below both moving averages, and the VIX has already re-spiked to 32.38 this morning. No new deployment until a zone is reclaimed and held, or a second low holds.

themes.counterRead: Index-level calm masks real weakness concentrated in the handful of names that dominate the index by weight — the rotation is genuine, but a rotation that keeps widening becomes a rollover if credit flips. Watch the Mag7-to-SPX gap, not the index level, for the turn.
themes.dataAnchor: The Mag7 averages 19.37% below their 52-week highs while SPX sits only 7.6% below its high — an 11.77-point gap, with AAPL just 3.3% off its high and NVDA 32.2% off. Bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% SLOOS, far below the ~40% stress threshold, and HY OAS is 3.76 with credit calm, not cracking. The index drawdown (-7.74% from its 120-day high of 7,844.52) is less than half the Mag7's.
themes.label: Index rotation, not rollover
themes.narrative: The tape reads as a broad crash: SPX is down 6.1% in a month, QQQ down 9.56%, and the VIX spiked to a 35.89 five-day high before Monday.
themes.watchFor: Mag7-to-SPX gap widening past 15 points, or HY OAS crossing 4.00.

themes.counterRead: The gap is the opportunity only if the multiple compression is sentiment rather than a demand break. NVDA's +31.48% single-day snap on the Huang reinstatement shows how fast the same fundamentals reprice — so entries need zone/bounce confirmation, not the dislocation alone.
themes.dataAnchor: NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% year over year while the stock sits 32.2% below its high; AVGO revenue +55% at -36.7%; CLS +66.8% at -55%; ONTO +41.5% at -50.6%; DDOG +27.7% revenue with an 80% gross margin and a 29.2% free-cash-flow margin at -43.8%. Of 36 dislocations, 18 are full signals and most are flagged SENTIMENT_DRIVEN, not fundamental, and insiders bought at the troughs: ROK $1.55M, VST $0.9M, ETN $0.32M, KTOS $0.2M.
themes.label: AI stack: fundamentals ahead of price
themes.narrative: AI is being sold as a busted trade, as if demand broke — the stack's drawdowns read as a verdict on the theme.
themes.watchFor: SMH and NVDA reclaiming Zone 2 (470-505 / 175-185) and holding it for two closes.

themes.counterRead: A first bounce is the precondition for a bottom, not the bottom itself — the confirmed-bottom pattern needs a failed first bounce and a second low that holds. Chasing this bounce into the failure zone (SMH 580-600, SPX 7,750-7,820) is the trap case.
themes.dataAnchor: The bounce had real mechanics behind it — SMH volume at 1.51x its 20-day average with a climax reversal, and the VIX rolling over to 26.62 from a 35.89 five-day high, putting the mechanical tally at 3 of 4. But SMH (460.18) and NVDA (165.05) both closed BELOW Zone 2 (470-505 / 175-185), SPX is still 4.99% below its 50-day and 1.54% below its 200-day, and this morning's live snapshot already shows the VIX back at 32.38, up 21.64% from Monday's close.
themes.label: First bounce, not a bottom
themes.narrative: Monday's +4.73% SPX, +15.03% SMH and +31.48% NVDA is being read as the bottom being in.
themes.watchFor: Whether SPX holds Monday's 7,237 close and SMH holds 460 on the retest.

themes.counterRead: Calm credit is what keeps this a CORRECTION rather than a regime break — but HY OAS has been widening steadily and the 4.00 line is the stand-down trigger. If credit cracks while equities bounce, the bounce is a trap, not a recovery.
themes.dataAnchor: HY OAS is 3.76, flagged calm with cracking false; bank lending standards are LOOSE at 1.7% SLOOS; the 2s10s curve is positively sloped at +0.29 with the 10-year at 4.92% and the real 10-year at 2.79%. Credit has not confirmed the equity drawdown at all.
themes.label: Credit calm while equities draw down
themes.narrative: The equity selloff implies a credit event is coming — the tape is pricing a funding break.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS crossing 4.00, or a second straight week of widening.

themes.counterRead: The leverage did exactly what leverage does in a 7.74% index drawdown — the damage is the position sizing talking, not a broken thesis. No adds to leveraged sleeves until the underlying (QQQ/SPX) confirms a bottom.
themes.dataAnchor: CONL is down 61.75% in a month, TQQQ down 30.77%, BMNR down 37.32%, DOGE down 26.93%, BTC down 22.34% and ETH down 25.55% — the leveraged and crypto sleeves took roughly three to six times the SPX's 6.1% monthly loss. The Nov 23 bounce (SPX +4.73%, SMH +15.03%) recovers only a fraction of a month like that.
themes.label: Leveraged sleeves took the damage
themes.narrative: Leveraged dip-buying pays on every bounce — the sleeves are where the recovery trade lives.
themes.watchFor: SMH and NVDA reclaiming Zone 2 — until then the leveraged sleeves stay sized as they are.

If instead credit cracks (HY OAS over 4.00) while equities bounce, the wave breaks the other way.
